image_description: A close-up shot of two white daisies with bright yellow centers against a background of green foliage. The top daisy is fully visible and in focus, while the bottom daisy is partially cut off by the frame edge. The lighting appears natural, casting soft shadows on the petals.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Composite flower with central yellow disc surrounded by single whorl of white ray petals.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The primary subject clearly exhibits the classic daisy structure: a distinct yellow central disc surrounded by a radial arrangement of white ray petals.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flower head is modest in size with numerous elongated white petals radiating outward.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The petals are elongated and radiate symmetrically from the center. The count appears consistent with typical daisy morphology (approx. 13-20 visible).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bright yellow center with bumpy, granular texture from individual disc florets.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The yellow center shows textural variation consistent with disc florets, rather than being a flat, uniform color block.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Petals narrow, slightly pointed, arranged in flat, circular pattern.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The white petals are narrow with rounded-to-slightly-pointed tips, arranged in a relatively flat plane.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Slender green stem supporting flower head.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The stems are largely occluded by the dense green foliage and the angle of the shot; no clear, isolated slender stem is visible connecting to the main flower head.

The image is a close-up of the flower heads; the ground level and stem bases are outside the frame or heavily occluded.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Some background leaves exhibit slight smearing or 'painterly' blending, lacking the crisp vein definition expected in high-resolution macro photography, though this may also be due to depth-of-field blur.
The lower edge of the bottom daisy merges slightly indistinctly with the background foliage, showing minor edge bleeding, but it is partially out of frame so severity is low.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species classification and rule out look-alikes like chamomile or shasta daisy based on petal/disc ratio.
To check for fusion between adjacent petals or bleeding into the background, common AI artifacts in floral generations.
To assess overall sharpness, noise patterns, and detect subtle generative inconsistencies in the foliage texture.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the boundary between the yellow disc and white petals. AI models often blur this transition or create irregular, non-circular discs. Also, verify if the petal counts are biologically plausible (not too few, not overlapping impossibly). Check if the background foliage has coherent structure or if it dissolves into abstract green blobs.
